Job Summary Quality Program Coordinator supports the planning, coordination, and evaluation of quality improvement initiatives, ensuring compliance with healthcare regulations while analyzing data, tracking performance, and aligning projects with organizational goals. Qualifications The Quality Program Coordinator role is responsible for supporting the planning, implementation, and monitoring of quality improvement projects. This role involves coordinating various quality initiatives, managing project timelines, and ensuring compliance with healthcare standards and regulations while working closely with clinical and administrative teams to enhance patient care quality, safety, and operational efficiency. The Quality Program Coordinator also functions as hospital's Patient Family Relations (PFR) lead, responding to patient and family complaints and grievances in accordance with regulations. Collects, organizes, and analyzes data related to quality measures, patient outcomes, and performance metrics. Fosters teamwork and partnerships between hospital staff, physicians, and department leaders, Quality, Risk, and Compliance to ensure responses are patient/family-centric. Provides telephone coverage and in-person support of patient and family relations for patients' and loved ones' needs, concerns, or complaints. Conducts rounds with patients, families, and visitors to obtain preemptive feedback regarding the inpatient hospital experience (when appropriate and aligned with hospital safety policies). Functions as the civil rights coordinator in receiving and coordinating follow-ups on any civil rights or health equity complaints. review_candidates.title: Investment Director
review_candidates.description: About the Company The Northern Australia Infrastructure Facility (NAIF) is a Commonwealth Government financier, providing financial support to advance the development of infrastructure projects in northern Australia and the Indian Ocean Territories. We help grow economies and populations and encourage private sector investment across a range of sectors including resources, agriculture and water, energy, financing partnerships, social infrastructure, and transport and logistics. We support projects that deliver public benefit to the north, through new jobs, regional income, business for local suppliers and Indigenous outcomes across northern Australia. NAIF has a $7 billion allocation of funds and has committed over $4.5 billion to support 35 projects in Queensland, Northern Territory and Western Australia. About the Opportunity The Investment Director works closely with the Chief Investment Officer as a key member of NAIF’s Investments leadership team. The role leads origination, execution and industry relationship activities across various sectors, manages complex transaction processes, and provides leadership and mentoring to investment team members. It plays an important role in building NAIF’s investment pipeline, strengthening market and government relationships, and progressing transactions in line with NAIF’s mandate, risk appetite and governance frameworks. Structuring, stakeholder engagement and clear credit paper narrative writing are core requirements of this role. NAIF has a strong preference to recruit employees based in Northern Australia, reflecting our purpose and the communities we serve. This role is ideally located in Cairns, however we will consider applicants from other locations where this supports securing the best candidate. Responsibilities Participating as a key member of the Investments leadership team, role modelling NAIF values and behaviours. Originating, structuring, negotiating and executing complex transactions, including preparation and presentation of credit submissions and Board papers. Leading and mentoring investment team members to support strong performance, effective deal execution and development of sector knowledge. Driving deal processes, timelines and outcomes across proponents, financiers, advisors, government stakeholders and internal teams. Building and maintaining strong relationships with key internal and external stakeholders, including government, proponents, equity investors, financiers and advisors. Developing business development and sector strategies, increasing market understanding of NAIF’s financing solutions and representing NAIF at targeted events and forums. Working collaboratively across NAIF to manage pipeline priorities, apply commercial acumen and support investment-related KPIs. About You At least 10 years’ experience in financial or related institutions, with experience in sophisticated origination, structuring and financial or credit analysis in project finance and/or corporate finance. Strong stakeholder influencing and management skills, with the ability to work effectively with clients, investors and financiers, government contacts, consultants and colleagues. Significant experience in a Director or senior leadership role within banking or financial services. Experience negotiating loan documentation and a strong understanding of complex financing agreements. Advanced documentation and structuring skills, with the ability to create clear, well-supported credit paper narratives. Excellent communication skills, including confidence presenting to internal and external stakeholders, Board meetings and industry forums. Highly organised, able to manage competing priorities, remain calm under pressure and deliver outcomes with minimal supervision. Experience leading, supporting, engaging and motivating high-performing team members. Why join NAIF? At NAIF, we are driven by our purpose and values. We foster a collaborative and supportive work environment, valuing the growth and development of our team members. We offer opportunities for professional development and prioritise the wellbeing of our staff. The successful applicant will be welcomed into a high performing team that is supportive, dedicated, knowledgeable, and passionate about our purpose of investing in the economic and social growth of northern Australia. How to apply? To apply for this position, please submit your resume and a cover letter outlining your relevant experience and how you align with NAIF's purpose and values. Applications should be submitted by 5:00pm, Monday 5 October 2026. Shortlisting may commence at any time.

review_candidates.title: Ingegnere di progetto
review_candidates.description: Descrizione del ruolo Ingegnere di progetto con sede di lavoro a Grisignano di Zocco, in ruolo full time e in presenza, sarà responsabile della gestione tecnica e organizzativa dei progetti assegnati. Nella giornata tipo, la persona si occuperà di analizzare i requisiti tecnici, elaborare soluzioni progettuali, predisporre la documentazione di progetto e coordinare le attività con il team interno e i fornitori. L’ingegnere di progetto seguirà l’avanzamento delle commesse, monitorando tempi, costi e qualità, e contribuendo alla risoluzione delle criticità operative. Il ruolo prevede il confronto costante con le altre funzioni aziendali e la partecipazione a riunioni tecniche, con attenzione alla sicurezza, alla conformità normativa e al miglioramento continuo dei processi. Qualifiche Il candidato deve possedere solide competenze in project engineering e project planning, con capacità di gestire attività complesse e coordinare le diverse fasi del progetto. È richiesta esperienza in project management, inclusa la pianificazione delle risorse, il controllo dei tempi e dei costi e la gestione dei rischi. Sono fondamentali competenze in electrical engineering, con conoscenza delle principali normative tecniche di settore e capacità di lettura di schemi e documentazione elettrica. Titolo di studio preferibile: laurea in ingegneria (elettrica, energetica o affini), buona padronanza degli strumenti informatici di progettazione e dei software di gestione progetti, attitudine al lavoro in team e orientamento al risultato.
